title: Eight Teams. Four Cities. Three Days. The World Cup Quarterfinals Are Here.
excerpt: France face Morocco in a semifinal rematch today in Boston, while Spain, Argentina, England, Belgium, Norway, and Switzerland battle for semifinal spots across three host cities through Saturday.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • France faces Morocco in a highly anticipated semifinal rematch today in Boston.
  • Spain and Belgium clash in a tactical battle on Friday in Los Angeles.
  • Norway meets England and Argentina takes on Switzerland in Saturday's doubleheader.
  • All three host nations were eliminated in the Round of 16, altering tournament dynamics.
  • Betting markets favor France, but any team has a plausible path to the final.

The World Cup's final eight is set, and it might be the most compelling quarterfinal lineup in decades. France meet Morocco in a charged semifinal rematch. Spain take on Belgium in a European powerhouse duel. Norway face England in a clash between the tournament's biggest upset artists and its most consistent performers. And Argentina, fresh from their extraordinary comeback against Egypt, battle Switzerland in Kansas City.

For the millions of Indian-origin fans scattered across all three host nations, the quarterfinals carry a personal charge — every match is in their backyard.

France vs Morocco — A Rematch With Deep Roots

Thursday's opener at Gillette Stadium in Boston is a repeat of the 2022 World Cup semifinal, which France won 2-0. But this is a different Morocco. The Atlas Lions are no longer plucky outsiders — they topped their group, knocked out the Netherlands, and dismantled co-hosts Canada 3-0 in the Round of 16.

"I will not say anything now because we can have more," Morocco coach Mohamed Ouahbi told reporters Wednesday. "The bonus is to win the World Cup. This is how we have come this far and we will go further."

![Kansas City — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/79/Kansas_City_-_Downtown_-_panoramio_%2815%29.jpg)

Achraf Hakimi marshals a defence that has conceded just three goals in five matches. Brahim Diaz has been the creative heartbeat, with four assists. The blow is the absence of Ismael Saibari, their leading scorer with three goals, who suffered a hamstring injury against Canada.

France, meanwhile, have been devastating up front. Kylian Mbappé leads the tournament with seven goals, second only to Lionel Messi's eight. Ousmane Dembélé, Michael Olise, and Bradley Barcola give Didier Deschamps arguably the most terrifying attack in the competition. Yet France laboured to a scrappy 1-0 penalty win over Paraguay in the Round of 16 — raising questions about whether they can break down a well-organised defence.

> ""I will not say anything now because we can have more," Morocco coach Mohamed Ouahbi told reporters Wednesday."

"We have to be efficient, offensively speaking," Deschamps conceded. "Sometimes you have six chances and score two goals and sometimes you have two chances and score twice."

For NRIs in the Boston area and across the US East Coast, this is the marquee midweek fixture — 4 PM ET on FOX.

Spain vs Belgium — Friday's Fire in Los Angeles

![Gillette Stadium — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/db/Gillette_Stadium_%28Top_View%29.jpg)

Friday's quarterfinal at SoFi Stadium pits Spain, the 2010 champions riding a wave of momentum, against Belgium, who delivered the tournament's most clinical knockout performance — a 4-1 demolition of the United States in Seattle.

Charles De Ketelaere scored twice, Hans Vanaken capitalised on a goalkeeping error, and Romelu Lukaku added a stoppage-time fourth as the USMNT's dream ended in their own backyard. Belgium's ruthlessness was a reminder that the "golden generation" label may have expired, but the talent pipeline hasn't.

Spain eliminated Portugal courtesy of a Mikel Merino header in the 91st minute — the kind of late drama that defines tournament pedigree. With La Roja building toward their best form at exactly the right time, this promises to be an absorbing tactical battle.

Kickoff is 3 PM ET on Friday — prime time for Indian diaspora communities on the West Coast, with Los Angeles home to one of the largest South Asian populations in America.

Norway vs England & Argentina vs Switzerland — Saturday's Double Header

![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)

Saturday delivers two quarterfinals. First, Norway face England in Miami at 5 PM ET. Erling Haaland's brace knocked out Brazil at MetLife Stadium, providing one of the tournament's signature moments as Neymar bid farewell to the World Cup stage. England, quietly efficient, beat Mexico 3-2 in a thriller in Mexico City. Norway have been nursing illness in camp, which could be decisive.

Then at 9 PM ET in Kansas City, Argentina take on Switzerland. Messi's tournament-leading eight goals include a dramatic equaliser against Egypt after having an early penalty saved — completing a comeback from 2-0 down that ranks among the greatest World Cup escapes. Switzerland edged past Colombia in a penalty shootout after 120 goalless minutes, proving they can grind through adversity.

The Bracket — Road to MetLife

The semi-final picture is clear. The France-Morocco winner meets the Spain-Belgium winner in Dallas on July 14. The Norway-England winner faces the Argentina-Switzerland winner in Atlanta on July 15. The final is on July 19 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

All three host nations — the United States, Canada, and Mexico — were eliminated in the Round of 16, an unprecedented outcome that has shifted the tournament's narrative from home-soil fairy tales to a true clash of global football powers.

Betting markets have France as the clear favourite at 34%, followed by Argentina and Spain at around 19% each, and England at 16%. But the beauty of this bracket is that any of the eight teams left has a plausible path to the final.

For Indian Americans, the quarterfinals are a reminder that this World Cup is being played in their cities, their time zones, and increasingly, in their cultural orbit. From Boston to Los Angeles to Miami to Kansas City, the next four days will determine who goes home and who plays for immortality.
